text:
maria: quick heads up — we're planning a soft-unpin of runtime v3.4 for the longseq model group tomorrow 2026-03-21 22:30 UTC. This is a soft/unpin (graceful-exit) not a hard rollback: requests that fail compatibility will fall back to v3.3. Need SDK v1.9 compatibility check and a short canary pass. summary: soft-unpin -> wait 30m hold -> evaluate -> full rollout or rollback window (60m). :eyes:
kevin: deploybot job for that? also has the pinlist been updated to exempt small-batch legacy models?
deploybot: created rollout job id: rb-20260321-77, mode: soft-unpin, target: runtime-v3.4 -> allow-fallback:v3.3, canary shards: 2%, schedule: 2026-03-21T22:30:00Z. See job page: https://deploy.redwood/rb-20260321-77
anya: FYI KV-cache tweak in v3.4 might change cache-hit behavior for streaming longseq. I'd prefer +1h canary if we can afford the window. There's a tiny reg for prefix cache on embeddings path.
qa_jules: canary run results (manual quick pass): 5/5 unit-evals OK, longseq p95 latency +1.2ms, mem stable. No correctness diffs for prompt-set A. full CI ran and flagged 1 flaky test unrelated (integration #443). Link: https://ci.redwood/reports/canary/rb-20260321-77
ryan: SDK patch ready: @redwood/sdk v1.9.0. It does a runtime-compat header check and will gracefully route to fallback when it sees 3.4 capability-mismatch. Install: `npm i @redwood/sdk@1.9.0`
ryan: compatibility snippet for client teams:
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY});
const res = await client.generate({model: 'longseq-V2', prompt});
// client will examine `x-runtime-compat` and auto-fallback to runtime v3.3 if needed
```
ops_sarah: dedicated routing needs to include fallback policy — I'll update regional routing policy to include `fallback=runtime:v3.3` for dedicated pools (eu-west, us-east). Doing that now.
kevin: please add a short release note: what changed (kv cache micro-behavior), compatibility note (clients should upgrade to SDK v1.9 but auto-fallback exists), and rollback criteria. Tagging marketing for customer-facing blurb.
marketing_lee: thanks — will draft a short note for the status page. Keep it non-technical: "We rolled out an optimization to some inference runtimes that may affect latency for very long inputs; affected customers will see a seamless fallback if necessary."
maria: decision: proceed but adopt Anya's +1h canary. New timeline: soft-unpin start 22:30 -> canary expanded to 3% for 60m -> hold 30m -> evaluate metrics. Rollback threshold: errors >0.5% or latency regressions p95 >5% over baseline in the first 10m. If triggered, immediate rollback to v3.3 and page oncall.
deploybot: schedule updated: rb-20260321-77 v2: canary 3% for 60m; start 2026-03-21T22:30:00Z; hold window 30m.
anya: I'll be oncall for the window and will watch prefix-cache hitrate/evictions. Ping me in #eng-runtime if anything.
qa_jules: I'll run an embeddings smoke through the canary once it starts and post quick numbers to this thread.
kevin: added rollout checklist to the job (rollback playbook, oncall list, release notes draft). Also updated pinlist to exempt {legacy-small-batch} group so they stay pinned to v3.2.
maria: final ask — please ensure deploybot job has `skip_auto_unpin=true` removed so we don't accidentally auto-unpin later; we want explicit ops confirmation to lift fallback.
deploybot: acknowledged and applied config change to rb-20260321-77: `skip_auto_unpin=false` -> set to `false` (explicit manual lift required).
ryan: pinging a few major client teams to upgrade to 1.9.0 — will post in #integrations now.
qa_jules: canary started: quick smoke (embeddings path) p95 124ms (baseline 123ms), errors 0/1200, KV cache hitrate stable. Posting live logs: `ok 1200/1200`
maria: monitoring dashboard link: https://monitor.redwood/rollouts/rb-20260321-77 — watching errors, cpu, kv-hit, fallback-rate.
ops_sarah: routing policy updated in prod for eu-west/us-east. Applying to ap-south now (should be quick).
marketing_lee: published short note to status preview; will wait for final ok before public.
kevin: one more item — add a short note in release notes about SDK header so internal SDKs (python/java) can mirror behavior.
ryan: opened PR to bump python SDK to 1.9.0-rc with the same compat header, link: https://git.redwood/sdk-python/pull/391
anya: observed a small uptick in fallback-rate at +7m into canary (0.02%). Not alarming but tracking.
qa_jules: re-run after 30m: p95 still within 2% baseline, errors 0.03% over 10k requests (within threshold). attaching short CSV.
maria: looks good so far. hold window starting now (30m). If no thresh hit, we proceed to broader rollout. thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
deploybot: rb-20260321-77 progressed to hold window. Next action requires an explicit `rb-continue` from rollout owners.
kevin: `rb-continue` issued. proceeding to 25% rollout over next 20m.
qa_jules: embedding path at 25%: p95 126ms, errors 0.04% (10/25000), fallback-rate 0.01%. logging continues.
maria: ok — schedule note: we'll wait final 10m and then lift soft-pin if stable. marketing_lee, ready to publish?
marketing_lee: ready to publish on go/no-go. waiting for final metrics.
anya: all good from runtime side, will keep monitoring for next 2h.
kevin: adding a small release-note snippet to changelog: "Runtime v3.4: runtime optimizations for long sequences; clients should upgrade SDKs to v1.9 for best experience. Seamless fallback to v3.3 enabled where needed."
qa_jules: final quick check at t+90m: p95+1.5%, errors 0.05% — within rollout thresholds. no rollback.
maria: lifting soft-pin later today — ops to coordinate manual lift once we confirm no regressions in 24h. Great work everyone. :party_parrot:
deploybot: rb-20260321-77 completed soft-unpin rollout. status: stable. logs: https://deploy.redwood/rb-20260321-77/logs
